:::{#rem-cramer-rao-scope}
#### What the bound does and does not say

The bound holds only for unbiased estimators,
and only when the regularity conditions of [the exercise on the mean of the score](intro-MLEs.qmd#exr-score-mean-zero) hold.
When the set of possible data values depends on the parameter,
as for the uniform distribution on $[0, \param]$,
the conditions fail and the bound need not hold
(compare [the uniform example](intro-MLEs.qmd#exm-information-equality-fails)).

A biased estimator can beat the bound,
because [mean squared error](estimation.qmd#thm-mse-bias-variance)
adds squared bias to the variance,
and trading a little bias for a large drop in variance
can lower the mean squared error.

The information from $n$ independent observations is $n$ times
the information from one,
so for a sample of size $n$ the bound shrinks like $1/n$.
That is the rate at which the variance of an efficient estimator falls,
and the [maximum likelihood estimator](intro-MLEs.qmd#thm-dist-mle)
attains it asymptotically.
:::
